the F3 gene contains multiple regulatory elements that are involved in the regulation of its expression in a cell type-specific, developmentally regulated, and hormone-dependent manner.
the F3 gene promoter is organized in a linear fashion and that it includes positive and negative regulatory elements.
F3 expression is controlled by a neural-specific enhancers located 1 kb upstream of the F3 transcription start site and by a cell-type-specific enhancer located within the 1st intron.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of cis- and trans-regulatory elements which govern the expression of F3 in the nervous system.
the identification and characterization of cis- and trans-acting elements involved in the regulation of F3 gene expression.
the functional characterization of the regulatory regions of the F3 axonal adhesion molecule gene and with the identification of the cis- and trans-acting factors involved in F3 expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

F3 is a neuron-specific gene which is regulated in a cell-type-specific manner by the interaction of a number of cis-acting elements with a set of trans-acting factors which include neural- and neuronal cell type-specific proteins.
the F3 gene promoter is built of a linearly arranged series of positive and negative elements, which are scattered throughout the 5' region of the F4 gene and the 5' exon (exon0).
the F3 gene promoter is organized as a mosaic of elements, some of which are involved in cell type-specific and others in cAMP and retinoid regulation of F3 transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the F3 gene promoter contains a complex organization of positive and negative cis-acting elements that are regulated by neural- and cell type- specific trans-acting factors and that are responsive to cAMP and retinoid signaling pathways.
F3 gene expression is controlled by the concerted action of a set of cis- and trans-acting factors, which act on the F3 promoter in a cell type-, developmental stage-, and signal-specific manner.
the F3 gene is under control of multiple cis-acting regulatory elements, each of which interacts with a specific combination of trans-acting factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the F3 gene promoter and exon 0 contain several elements that are involved in the regulation of F3 gene expression by a number of different signals, including cell type, developmental stage, and environmental cues.
the organization of F3 gene regulatory elements is complex.
the F3 gene promoter is a composite of multiple elements that interact with specific trans-acting proteins.
